info.name: DalMarketplace API
info.description:
API collection for the DalMarketplace backend (Express + Firestore).

Usage:
1. Set the `baseUrl` collection variable (default http://localhost:5000).
2. Run **Auth > Signup** once to create a user (email must end in @dal.ca).
3. Run **Auth > Login** — its test script saves the JWT into the `token` variable automatically.
4. All protected requests (e.g. Listings > Create Listing) then send `Authorization: Bearer {{token}}`.

**Error shape (consistent across the whole API):**
```
{ "error": "<message>", "details": ["..."] }
```
`error` is always a human-readable string. `details` is only present for validation errors (an array of field problems). 5xx errors are rendered as `{ "error": "Internal server error" }` (internal messages are not leaked). Saved examples below show each case.

request.description: Register a new user. Email must end in @dal.ca. Returns the created userId.

exec: // Save the JWT and identity so protected requests can reuse them.
pm.test('error responses use { error: string }', () => pm.expect(res.error).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: Authenticate by Banner ID + password. On success, the test script stores `token` and `userId` as collection variables.

Create a listing (requires auth). Server validates required fields and derives the seller from the token, not the body. `status: "published"` is normalized to `available`. category/condition/region must match the allowed enums.
Demonstrates server-side validation: returns 400 with a `details` array listing each problem.

response.name: 400 Validation failed

request.description:
Requires auth (Bearer token). Paginated browse of published (`available`) listings, ordered newest-first. Cursor pagination: send `limit` and, for subsequent pages, `cursor` set to the `nextCursor` returned previously. `nextCursor` is `null` on the last page.

Note: this query needs a Firestore composite index on `status` (asc) + `createdAt` (desc); Firestore logs a one-click link to create it on the first call.

query.description: Optional. Case-insensitive prefix match on the listing title (e.g. `led` matches "LED Monitor"). Omit to browse/filter without a text query.
Optional equality filter — one of the CATEGORIES enum.
Optional equality filter — one of the REGIONS enum.
Optional equality filter — one of the CONDITIONS enum.
Optional minimum price (inclusive). Applied in memory.
Optional maximum price (inclusive). Applied in memory.
Optional sort: `recent` (default), `price_asc`, or `price_desc`. Applied in memory.
Pass the `nextOffset` from the previous page to fetch the next one.

request.description:
Requires auth (Bearer token). Search + filter over published (`available`), non-deleted listings. When `q` is present, it's a case-insensitive prefix match on the lowercased `title_lower` field (Firestore has no full-text search); when omitted, results are ordered newest-first.

`category` / `region` / `condition` are native equality filters. `minPrice` / `maxPrice` and `sort` (`recent` | `price_asc` | `price_desc`) are applied in memory over a candidate window (up to 500 docs), because Firestore can't combine a title prefix range with a price range or arbitrary sort in one indexed query. Pagination is offset-based: the response returns `total` and `nextOffset` (`null` on the last page).

Note: needs Firestore composite indexes (category/region/condition subsets for both the `title_lower` and `createdAt` order paths), defined in `firestore.indexes.json`; deploy with `firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes`. Until deployed the query 500s with a one-click index-creation link in the server logs.

request.description:
Requires auth (Bearer token). The authed user's own listings across every status — including `draft`, `reserved`, and `sold` — excluding soft-deleted ones, ordered newest-first. Powers the seller dashboard (unlike `GET /api/listings`, which only returns `available` listings). Cursor pagination via `nextCursor` (a `createdAt` value), `null` on the last page.

Note: needs a Firestore composite index on `sellerId` + `isDeleted` + `createdAt` (in `firestore.indexes.json`).

request.description: Edit a listing — owner only. Partial body allowed (only sends fields you include; validated with `validateListing({ partial: true })`). Re-checks ownership against the token: 403 if you don't own it, 404 if it's missing or soft-deleted.
Set the sale status — owner only. `status` must be one of `available`, `reserved`, `sold` (400 otherwise). 403 if not the owner, 404 if missing/soft-deleted.

response.name: 400 Invalid status

request.description: Soft delete — owner only. Does NOT remove the document; it sets `isDeleted: true` + `deletedAt`, so the listing disappears from browse (`GET /api/listings`) and detail (`GET /api/listings/:id` then 404s). 403 if not the owner. Calling it again 404s (already deleted).

Submit a star rating (1–5) + comment for a seller (requires auth; reviewer is taken from the token). Preconditions the server enforces:
- The listing (`listingId`) must exist, belong to `sellerId`, and be `status: "sold"`.
- You cannot review yourself (`sellerId` must differ from your own userId).
- One review per reviewer per listing — the review doc id is `reviewerId_listingId`, so a repeat returns 409.

On success it atomically writes the review and updates the seller's denormalized `ratingAvg` + `ratingCount`. Set the `sellerId` and `listingId` collection variables to a sold listing owned by another user before running.
